clue.text: Rest of question I study in music

indicators.note: places the study inside the field of music, telling you which kind of study is meant

parts.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
taken as it stands
an étude is a musical study

explanation.surface: A music student pauses for a breather between questions and practice.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rest" looks like a musical pause alongside "music", but it is the calm meaning, a noun like QUIETUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a literary word for a state of stillness and repose.

parts.note: Los Angeles, the Californian city
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the newest cricket game played in California.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a long international cricket match; the question mark flags how odd cricket in California would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the newest news or fashion is described this way.

indicators.note: puts the word for permitted inside the word for road

parts.note: a route is a road
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A question about which games may legally be played in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: "In road?" suggests a street game; the question mark warns that the phrase is an instruction, not scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the casino game where a ball settles on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Betting figures on Derby Day shown only for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first letters, so take only those

parts.note: first letters of On, Derby, Day, Shown

explanation.surface: Bookmakers display their prices at the start of the big horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race, so betting odds belong in the scene; "shown" supplies a letter as well as joining.
explanation.definitionFit: The prices bookmakers offer, such as five to one, are called by this word.

clue.text: Become obsessed with God's will holding team up

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: fate is what the gods decree

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read the letters bottom to top

parts.note: a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A fanatic becomes fixated on divine will propping up their team.
explanation.walkthrough: XI (Roman eleven) is a standard way to clue a team; it turns to IX inside FATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to fix one's attention on something to an unhealthy degree.

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A river's force is hard to fathom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a profound idea, like deep water, is hard to get to the bottom of.

indicators.note: in crosswords, over means turned back

parts.note: An is the article A
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a tuba.
explanation.walkthrough: A then BUT reads ABUT; turned over it becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest, lowest-pitched member of the brass family.

definitions.meaning: as a noun, an ancient is an elderly person, a veteran
a clepsydra, an antique device for measuring time

explanation.surface: A water clock from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ancient" is a noun here, an old person; the question mark flags reading OLD TIMER literally as an old device for timing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient, as a noun, is an elderly person; read literally, a water clock is an aged timekeeping device.

clue.text: Annul a law initially after peer's upset

indicators.note: take only the first letter of law
peer is knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: PEER rearranged
taken as it stands
first letter of law

explanation.surface: A lord, upset, wants a law struck off.
explanation.walkthrough: A peer is a member of the House of Lords, which can vote to annul laws.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: formally revoking a law or ruling so it no longer applies.

indicators.note: the agent grabs the sleep and holds it inside

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A tired secret agent turns grumpy after snatching some sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: "Agent" could be an estate or sports agent; in crosswords it is nearly always a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short-tempered person snaps at others.

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: QUITE, meaning completely, without its final E

explanation.surface: Someone walks out for good and clocks off early.
explanation.walkthrough: "Completely" looks like part of the definition, but it is the wordplay: QUITE cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: walking out of a job or place for good.

clue.text: Cross and abrupt about endless wild party

indicators.note: the party loses its last letter

parts.note: terse means curt, abrupt
a rave is a wild party; without its end it is RAV

explanation.surface: Someone is angry and curt about a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cross" looks like the adjective angry, which suits "abrupt"; it is the verb, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go across something, such as a ridge or a room.

clue.text: Cause of bad lighting on stairs must be changed

indicators.note: the letters of on stairs are to be changed around

parts.note: ONSTAIRS rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice that the dim lights on the staircase need replacing.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bad lighting" reads as poor illumination; here it means lighting a fire with bad intent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone who sets fires on purpose causes a bad kind of lighting.

parts.note: the hyphens show a word said letter by letter, the ordinary sense
a witch works magic with charms and incantations, the setter's second sense

explanation.surface: Someone talks letter by letter, in the manner of a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated letters show words being spelt out, while a witch is someone who spells in the magic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming a word's letters in order, as the hyphens show, and also a witch's casting of charms.

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: SNAKESWE rearranged

explanation.surface: We startled some snakes and learned how fragile they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pins the frailty on the snakes, but "Frailty" stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lack of strength or a flaw of character.

clue.text: Report of what could be black chess piece

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the answer sounds like the word

parts.note: the night can be black

explanation.surface: Talk of a dark piece on the chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: "Black" suggests the chess side; it describes the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chess piece shaped like a horse's head.

indicators.note: keep only half the word, here its back half

parts.note: completed is FINISHED; keep only its back four letters

explanation.surface: A small building project is only halfway done.
explanation.walkthrough: The half kept is the back one: FINI goes, the rest stays.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small wooden outbuilding for tools or storage.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cabby drives a cab

explanation.surface: A passenger's verdict on the second cab driver they met.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabby is an informal British word for a taxi driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal: literally covered in scabs, figuratively mean and contemptible.

clue.text: A large tree in the mountains

parts.note: taken as it stands
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: A big tree growing high up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase acting as an adjective, as the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: found high in mountains, originally the Alps.

clue.text: Fruit somewhere between ugli and melon

indicators.note: take the letters either side of the gap between the fruits: the end of one and the start of the other

parts.note: the last two letters of ugli
the start of melon: its first letter and the one after

explanation.surface: A fruit whose size or taste falls between an ugli fruit and a melon.
explanation.walkthrough: It works like a word spanning two words but skips "and": the answer sits where ugli meets melon. An ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small green citrus fruit.

clue.text: A piece of cake? Queen's left nauseous

indicators.note: has left, meaning departed from the word

parts.note: QUEASY is nauseous; QU for Queen departs

explanation.surface: Someone asks for cake, but the Queen has gone off feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: QU is a standard abbreviation for Queen. "Queen's left" means Queen has left; "a piece of cake" is slang for a simple task.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a piece of cake is a task needing no effort at all.

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
as in advance warning, meaning early

explanation.surface: Something is close to being a fresh step forward.
explanation.walkthrough: "Advance" is the adjective, as in advance booking, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: very close to happening or being true, but not quite.

clue.text: Special importance of the mph as I speed?

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the words that follow

parts.note: thE MPH AS I Speed

explanation.surface: A driver asks why the speedometer reading matters so much as they speed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of "the" to the first letter of "speed".
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: extra weight or stress laid on something.

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Offering a nice cake to win someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: This is British slang, common in football and politics reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a backhander, money slipped to someone to win a favour.
